rows.notes: The paper is a discussion/perspective piece (Section 1 states it 'discusses an integrated water resource management approach'; Sections 4-5 review previously developed remote sensing methods, government reports and surveys by others). Table 1 is adapted from MDBA (2017b), not the authors' own data. No own experiment, survey, measurements or validated model runs are reported, so it is not a primary study. The claimed effect (remote sensing improving management of irrigation water use/groundwater extraction in a sanctioning context) is argued from cited work (Bretreger et al. 2019, 2020; MDBA 2017a, 2018a, 2019a; Krause and Reinfelds 2020), not from results of this paper.

Not a primary study. The statements about NSW NRAR, satellite-based investigations (MDBA 2019a first-flush report sent to NRAR, Waterbodies tool) and increased prosecutions are drawn from government reports, media articles and Carmody (2018), and are presented as narrative in Sections 3, 4.2.1 and 5.2.1 and as 'Enabler #4'. The paper reports no own data or analysis demonstrating that institutional investment in technology and governance closed enforcement gaps.

notes: The document is a discussion/perspective paper on compliance in the Murray-Darling Basin, synthesising government reports, media and prior studies (including the authors' own earlier remote sensing papers, which are cited but not reported here). It presents five policy 'enablers' as recommendations. Full text appears complete.
